notes: Captured 2026-11-19 from T3 Code v0.1.11 by an MCP client signed in from outside a thread with a full-access token, using scratch threads, projects, and scheduled tasks that the capture probe created and then archived or deleted; no user data.

Thread-only tools (task_status, create_threads, preview_open) are not listed for MCP clients signed in from outside a thread (tools/list returns 53 tools); calling one fails with JSON-RPC -32602 "Tool '<name>' not found".
A pending user question leaves the thread status 'running'; pendingRequestCount on the thread detail becomes > 0.

t3_thread_read without a position pages from the start, oldest first. Its default view is 'messages' (user and assistant messages only); view 'activity' adds command_execution, checkpoint, and other items, so positions in the messages view have gaps.
afterPosition is exclusive; afterPosition -1 reads from the start.

beforePosition N returns up to limit items just before position N, in ascending order. earlierPosition is the first returned item's position when earlier items exist, otherwise null; it is present on every read. nextPosition is the last returned position, and a beforePosition page reports hasMore true when later items exist.
Reads that pass afterPosition or beforePosition return a thread detail without pullRequests and openPullRequestCount; pullRequestCount stays.
t3_thread_list rows carry no branch key (none of 60 rows had one); the thread detail still carries branch.

Interrupting a running turn ends that run 'interrupted' (0.1.8 also observed 'cancelled', depending on timing). A queued run that is cancelled stays the thread's latestRunId, so t3_thread_wait without runId returns that cancelled run at once and the thread status reads 'cancelled' even while the interrupted run is still winding down.
Archiving also settles (the archived thread reads archived true, settled true); archived threads disappear from t3_thread_list.
clientRequestId makes t3_thread_launch, t3_thread_update, and schedule_task idempotent (same ids returned); t3_thread_send idempotency is carried over from 0.1.8 unverified.
401 WWW-Authenticate carries resource_metadata unless the presented token is non-empty without a '.', and error="invalid_token" whenever a token was presented; real MCP client tokens contain a '.'.
t3_project_create ignores defaultModelSelection (the result is always null); set it with t3_project_update, which stores {instanceId, model} plus options and drops provider.

schedule_task accepts a project without a default model (schedule_task.projectWithoutDefaultModel). Both scheduled runs ran claudeAgent / claude-fable-5-2 although their projects' default model was claude-haiku-5-5, so the run model does not come from the project default. Outside callers are never bound (boundThreadId null); clientRequestId makes creation idempotent.

Only schedule_task creation returns webhookUrl (with T3 Connect on). Update results and list_scheduled_tasks rows carry webhookSignature but not webhookUrl. list_scheduled_tasks accepts scheduledTaskId to return one task.

run_scheduled_task_now works on disabled tasks, starts a new full-access thread in the task's project, and reports lastRunStatus 'succeeded' with lastRunError null once started. In a git project the run gets a new worktree under ~/.t3/worktrees/<project>/; in a project whose folder is not a git repository it ran in place (worktreePath null) and completed.
t3_project_clone with provider and repository cloned over SSH (remoteUrl is the SSH URL) with protocol left at auto.
orchestrator_capabilities providers and models are trimmed here; the real catalog lists more of both.

Carried over from 0.1.8 unverified: the note that run status 'waiting' counts as running and that t3_pending_request does not list approvals; the note that deleting a project with threads needs force: true and leaves the folder on disk; results.scheduledRun.failedThreadDetail and errors.scheduledRun.notGitRepository (on 0.1.11 the same setup completed, see scheduledRun.nonGitRepositoryThreadDetail); cli.env.

Phase 3 samples (pull requests, t3_thread_configure, t3_thread_transfer, t3_worktree_list, t3_project_read, t3_environment_links) were captured 2026-11-19 from T3 Code v0.1.11-nightly.20261118.4890 by an outside client holding the bridge's pairing credential, on a scratch thread that was archived afterwards.
An outside client has the orchestration, worktree, and pull-requests capabilities and no calling thread: these tools need threadId, and the pull-request tools refuse without one in plain text.
link_pull_requests lower-cases the repository in its result and keeps the URL as given; a linked pull request has state null until T3 reads it from its host (about four seconds here).
watch_pull_request links first when needed and refuses only a merged pull request; a closed one is accepted. With repository and number, a thread whose project has no git remote also needs host.
unlink_pull_requests unlinks by last known state; unwatch_pull_request on a pull request that was never linked succeeds and links nothing.
t3_thread_configure rejects an unknown provider instance and accepts an unknown model id.

A fork is idle, carries relationshipToParent 'fork' and its source as parentThreadId, and keeps the source's model and modes; its transfer stays 'pending' and is listed for source and target. merge_back from a thread without a finished run fails.
